page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.48xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processors. It features 192 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz with a single thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 768 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with 11,400 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the m9gd.48xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance. Multi-core stress-ng tests, Passmark CPU scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all rank in the top 10% of tested systems. The memory subsystem also achieves top-tier status, with read-only cached bandwidth reaching 27,785.94 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth at 327.45 GB/sec. Single-core performance is more moderate, placing in the middle 50% for stress-ng single-core tests.

This instance is highly optimized for data-intensive and concurrent workloads. It achieves top-tier results in database operations, processing 506.95 million Redis SET operations per second, and delivers 358.31 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. The combination of high-density ARMv9 cores and massive local NVMe storage provides high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for large-scale databases, web serving, and multi-threaded data processing. However, the lack of hardware accelerators makes it less suitable for heavy LLM text generation, where it shows average to poor performance.
